vo: Every design has a footprint. Energy, devices, materials, and attention. Most of it is locked in early, before anyone thinks to measure it. Design Impact Plan is a Claude Code skill that brings those questions to the very start of the work.

It's built on two thinkers. From Don Norman's Design for a Better World: humanity-centered design. Solve the root problem, consider the whole ecosystem, think long term, and design with communities. From Buckminster Fuller's Critical Path: anticipate instead of react, do more with less, and look for the trimtab, the small change that turns the whole ship.

Ask Claude for an impact plan, and the skill works through six steps. It understands the design, maps the system and its critical path, runs the lifecycle, behavior, and community lenses, finds the trimtabs, translates fixes into design tokens, and writes a short plan you can share.

Every plan ends in one honest verdict: build, build differently, reconsider, or don't build. Impacts are rated high, medium, or low, with a confidence level. Carbon numbers only appear when they come from a named method, with the inputs shown. And accessibility is never traded away for efficiency.

Here's a real plan from testing. A homepage hero with autoplay video and parallax, at two million visits a month. The verdict: build differently. The top trimtab: make a still poster the default, and play the video only where it's cheap and welcome. Decided before the shoot, while it's still easy to change.

It handles phygital work too. For smart skincare packaging with an NFC chip in every jar, it recommends a printed QR code instead. And it catches a risk the plain model missed: a brand-owned redirect, so half a million jars don't turn into dead links.
When a fix is systemic, it belongs in the design system. A reduced motion mode. Parallax depth set to zero. Media budgets for each breakpoint. Change it once, and every future design inherits it.
In side-by-side tests, plans made with the skill passed all twenty-one checks. Without it, sixteen. The difference is discipline: one clear verdict, leverage first, and no unsourced numbers.
To try it, open the design tokens repo in Claude Code, and ask for an impact plan for whatever you're designing next. Design for a better world, one decision at a time.
